title: Sections and canonical completion comparisons in the explicit cone model
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a strict tower $X_\bullet$ with transitions $w_n$ set $s_X((x_n)_n)=(w_nx_{n+1})_n$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For every strict tower $X_\bullet$ of complexes of $R$-modules, there is a specified chain isomorphism
$$c_X:\Gamma H(X_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(\Gamma X_\bullet)$$
which is the sectionwise product identification on both displayed components. For every strict tower map $w:X_\bullet\to Y_\bullet$, $H(w)$ is the chain map $(b,a)\mapsto((\prod_nw_n)b,(\prod_nw_n)a)$, and $c_Y\Gamma H(w)=H(\Gamma w)c_X$. These cones represent the derived inverse limits [def-weil-derived-limit] of the whole strict towers. The maps $c_X$ descend through levelwise quasi-isomorphisms and remain natural there.

Let $N\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and let $q:P\to N$ be any flat-term K-flat resolution. Put $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$, $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$, $D_n=\Gamma P_n$ and $B_n=\Gamma C_n$, with their actual quotient transitions [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. The identity-extension completion map $\chi_N:N\to H(P_\bullet)$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] and the defining cone representative $Lg^*N\simeq H(C_\bullet)$ of completed pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] induce specified isomorphisms
$$\alpha_N:\Gamma N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(D_\bullet),\qquad \beta_N:\Gamma Lg^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(B_\bullet).$$
On $P$, $\alpha_N\Gamma(q)$ is represented by $a_P:z\mapsto(0,(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$; $\beta_N$ uses $c_C$, the identity on both sectionwise product components. The codomains are respectively $R\lim_n\Gamma(N_n)$ and $R\lim_n\Gamma(Lg_n^*N_n)$. These specified comparisons are independent of the flat-term K-flat resolution under its derived comparison maps, and are natural for every derived morphism of integral constructible inputs. No comparison chosen merely from an unspecified Roos triangle is included in these assertions.

proof.text: Put $V_X=\prod_nX_n$ termwise. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], evaluation at $s$ identifies $\Gamma(V_X)^i$ with $\prod_n\Gamma(X_n^i)$, with the actual product projections. In these identifications, the $n$-th component of $\Gamma(s_X)$ is $\Gamma(w_n)\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$, hence $\Gamma(1-s_X)=1-s_{\Gamma X}$. Exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] are additive and preserve binary biproducts. Define $c_X^i$ by these identifications on the two summands $V_X^{i-1}\oplus V_X^i$. Both summand identifications are invertible, so $c_X^i$ is invertible.

proof.text: Under $c_X$, the differential applied to $(b,a)$ is $(-\Gamma(d)b-(1-s_{\Gamma X})a,\Gamma(d)a)$ on either side, so the componentwise isomorphisms are a chain isomorphism. For a strict tower map $w:X\to Y$, put $W=\prod_nw_n$. Strict compatibility gives $(1-s_Y)W=W(1-s_X)$. The diagonal map $(b,a)\mapsto(Wb,Wa)$ therefore commutes with the displayed differentials; its identity and composition laws hold on both components. Evaluating this map at $s$ gives precisely the diagonal map built from $\prod_n\Gamma(w_n)$, proving $c_Y\Gamma H(w)=H(\Gamma w)c_X$. This uses the signed cone coordinates and strict cone-map construction of [def-weil-strict-roos-model].

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit sectionwise refinement of blueprint prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model, proof (3)

proof.text: The source sheaf-module category has exact countable products by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. The target module category does too: products are Cartesian products with componentwise action, and a product of surjections is surjective by choosing a lift in each coordinate. Apply [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] in both categories. Thus the termwise products used above represent products of the entire complexes in their derived categories, with no boundedness or Mittag--Leffler assumption. The shifted cone triangle of $1-s$ is distinguished by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so it exhibits $H(X)$ and $H(\Gamma X)$ as the derived limits of their whole towers in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit].

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit sectionwise refinement of blueprint prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model, proof (3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] to the source module-sheaf category and to ordinary modules viewed as sheaves on the one-object site with trivial topology. Its exact-product hypothesis was checked in Step 3. Its descent assertion says that the strict cone construction inverts levelwise quasi-isomorphisms of tower complexes. Sections also preserve quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], levelwise and on the resulting cones. Consequently both sides of $c_X$ invert these maps. The equality of Step 2 descends by the localization defining the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: if $v:X\to X'$ is inverted, $c_{X'}\Gamma H(v)=H(\Gamma v)c_X$ also implies the corresponding square for $v^{-1}$ by multiplication with the two inverses. Composition then gives naturality for localized tower morphisms. No identification of arbitrary separately chosen Roos triangles is used.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit sectionwise refinement of blueprint prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model, proof (3)

proof.text: For the fixed flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to N$, the complexes $P_n$ compute $N_n=N\otimes_R^L(A_n)_s$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], applied to the projections $R\to(A_n)_s$. At finite coefficients, [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] specifies that $Lg_n^*$ is computed by exact termwise module inverse image on any representative. Thus $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$ computes the finite pullback, with the actual quotient transitions specified in the same definition. Applying exact sections computes $\Gamma(N_n)$ and $\Gamma(Lg_n^*N_n)$ by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Step 3 now identifies $H(D)$ and $H(B)$ with the two derived-limit codomains asserted in the item. This uses one strict representative of each entire tower, not just a list of isomorphisms between separate levels.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit sectionwise refinement of blueprint prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model, proof (3)

proof.text: Specialize [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to the identity extension $L=E$, $Y=s$, $K=N$. Its completeness hypothesis is exactly the derived completeness assumed here, and it gives a specified natural isomorphism $\chi_N:N\to H(P_\bullet)$, independent of the resolution. Define $\alpha_N=c_{P_\bullet}\Gamma(\chi_N)$. Sections preserve isomorphisms, so this is an isomorphism. That lemma specifies $\chi_Nq$ as the augmentation with zero shifted-product component and product component $(r_n)_n$. Since $c_P$ is the sectionwise identification, $\alpha_N\Gamma(q)$ is represented by $a_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$. In particular it is the specified map, including its sign and zero component. Directly, $(1-s_D)(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n=0$ because each quotient transition carries $r_{n+1}$ to $r_n$, so the displayed formula commutes with the differential.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit sectionwise refinement of blueprint prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model, proof (3)

proof.text: Write $\iota_{g,N}:Lg^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(C_\bullet)$ for the representative comparison in the defining integral pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define $\beta_N=c_{C_\bullet}\Gamma(\iota_{g,N})$. This is an isomorphism, and on the chosen model $H(C)$ its sectionwise map is exactly $c_C$, the identity under both product identifications. The comparison $\iota_{g,N}$ is the comparison with the explicit complex supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], whose statement gives descent to functors and independence of resolutions with these very comparison maps. Thus this construction fixes $\beta_N$ without making a choice from a Roos triangle.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; explicit sectionwise refinement of blueprint prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model, proof (3)

proof.text:
The identity-extension maps $\chi_N$ are natural for derived morphisms and independent of resolutions by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The completed pullbacks and their representative comparisons have the same properties by [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Combine these two assertions with the localized naturality of $c$ from Step 4. Explicitly, for a derived morphism $f:N\to N'$, let $D(f)$ and $B(f)$ denote the maps on the evaluated reduction and pullback towers induced by those descended constructions. Composition of the two naturality squares gives
$$H(D(f))\alpha_N=\alpha_{N'}\Gamma(f),\qquad H(B(f))\beta_N=\beta_{N'}\Gamma(Lg^*f).$$
For a change of flat-term K-flat resolution the same equations apply with the canonical comparison maps, so the two definitions agree under those maps. Naturality for an inverse quasi-isomorphism follows by multiplying the chain-map square by its inverses, and hence holds for every derived morphism. This proves independence and naturality with the specified strict-cone comparisons throughout.
